newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ICN founds Macedonia joint venture.
newsitem.headline: ICN founds Macedonia joint venture.

text.p: ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc and Ohis of Macedonia have set up a joint venture company for the production and marketing of medicines, ICN Yugoslavia said in a press release on Monday.
The California-based parent company will have a 75 percent stake and Ohis 25 percent in the new Skopje-based enterprise which will operate under the name ICN Macedonia.

The contract for the new venture, which is expected to begin production and sale of medicines within six months, was signed in Skopje by ICN Pharmaceuticals President Milan Panic and Ohis general manager Jorgo Cuka.
"Our goal is to produce high quality medicines at acceptable prices for the Macedonian market, and I think we will succeed in that," Panic said at the signing.
Cuka said the investment of U.S. capital in the Macedonian pharmaceutical industry would help its further development.

"ICN, which this year acquired two pharmaceutical plants in Russia and one in Hungary, is completing its expansion in eastern Europe by covering the markets of former Yugoslavia," the ICN press release said.

The U.S. company recently signed agreements with the Montenegrin government to found ICN Montenegro in Podgorica and with the Bosnian Serb government to found a joint limited liability company ICN Krajinalek in Banja Luka.

ICN Yugoslavia, set up as a joint venture with the Belgrade-based firm Galenika in 1991, earlier said 1996 annual sales were expected to reach nearly $350 million, of which exports would account for some $50 million. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
